title: Gleam doesn't compile to Erlang source anymore
why_read: A significant compiler architecture change in Gleam affecting how the language targets the BEAM VM is genuinely useful for language implementers and Erlang/Elixir-adjacent developers.
analysis: Gleam is a statically typed language that compiles to the Erlang VM, and this post describes a shift away from generating literal Erlang source code as an intermediate step. This kind of change usually brings better compile times, more direct control over generated bytecode, and fewer impedance mismatches between Gleam's type system and Erlang's dynamic runtime. It's a solid, technical post likely explaining real compiler engineering tradeoffs rather than hype. Relevant to anyone interested in language design or the BEAM ecosystem.
